Article Title: Make govt sites user-friendly, PM Modi tells mantris
Article Text:
PM pushes for one-login govt portal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Wednesday is learnt to have told ministers to make govt websites “user-friendly” to access information about welfare schemes and public services easily, and has advised Cabinet colleagues to be assertive while dealing with those who have made it their business of levelling unfair and baseless criticism.PM’s direction to Cabinet ministers on improving govt portals comes barely months after cabinet secretary T V Somanthan advised all ministries and departments to overhaul their websites to make them easier to navigate. At the last council of ministers’ meeting, attended by all Union secretaries, Somanathan had referred to a report by The Economist that had flagged how govt websites in India remain difficult for ordinary citizens to use.The report said that govt portals are cluttered with pop-ups, flashing banners and scrolling text, to name a few. It had also said that several websites work poorly on mobile phones despite most Indians using the internet through mobile phones.Recently, PM had directed the electronics and IT ministry to expedite the “Ek Bharat” portal, a unified service delivery platform for citizens which will require people to access all govt websites with just one username and password.TOI has learned that many saw the PM’s advice to ministers about being assertive to counter a negative campaign as a reference to “naaraz fufa”. Sources said govt has achievements to highlight to effectively counter negative narratives.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi has told ministers to make govt websites ‘user-friendly’ he has advised cabinet colleagues to be assertive while dealing with those who have made it their business of levelling unfair and baseless criticism. Article Title: Australian space firms seek deeper India partnerships
Article Text:
The University of Western Australia and the Space Industry Association of India intend to collaborate through the university's Global Engagement Alliance, focusing on education, research and industry engagement and the exchange of expertise and opportunities.

BENGALURU: A 12-member Australian space industry delegation led by the Australian Trade and Investment Commission (Austrade) used Bengaluru Space Expo 2026 to explore commercial partnerships with Indian companies across the space and adjacent technology sectors.Nathan Davis, Trade and Investment Commissioner, Austrade, India, said the delegation was aimed at taking Australia-India space cooperation into a “next commercial chapter”, with Australian companies bringing capabilities that complement India's scale and expanding space ecosystem.Australia, one of the Tech Country partners at the ninth edition of the expo which ended Wednesday, showcased capabilities spanning launch and return services, Earth observation, bio-inspired sensing, cold spray additive manufacturing, space biology and microgravity research, in-space servicing software, space radiation testing, electric propulsion, space and AI research, radio astronomy, and advanced communications and data-intensive technologies.“The delegation's visit is supported by the Australian Space Agency, Invest and Trade Western Australia, the Government of Western Australia and the Space Industry Association of Australia. It is part of the Australian Government's Accessing New Markets Initiative and South Asia Business Exchange programme,” an official statement read.Several potential partnerships between Australian and Indian organisations are also being advanced at the expo.Australian Earth observation company LatConnect 60 (LC60) and Isro’s commercial arm NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) are entering into an agreement under which LC60's SWIRSAT mission will access NSIL’s ground-station infrastructure in India for mission operations and data downlink requirements.The University of Western Australia and the Space Industry Association of India intend to collaborate through the university's Global Engagement Alliance, focusing on education, research and industry engagement and the exchange of expertise and opportunities.Australia's Space Angel Group and India's Inbound Aerospace have established the sustainability of Space Angel's spaceports for recovering Inbound's autonomous, resuable capsule and returned microgravity payloads, with the two companies now working through technical details and the return authorisation pathway as they progress toward definitive commercial agreements.Space Angel is also collaborating with Red Balloon Aerospace on future commercial missions, including the return of spacecraft and resources obtained from asteroids and other celestial bodies. Separately, it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Andura Expeditions covering spacecraft testing, spaceport activities, high-altitude drop-test campaigns and hypersonic recovery.The delegation has also undertaken site visits and meetings with Indian companies to understand the country's space ecosystem.
Article Summary: A 12-member australian space industry delegation used bengaluru space expo 2026 to explore commercial partnerships with indian companies. The delegation was aimed at taking australia-india space cooperation into a ‘next commercial chapter’ the university of western australia and the space industry association of india intend to collaborate through the university's global engagement alliance.

Article Title: Beyond E20? Only flex-fuel vehicles may have the option, indicates adviser
Article Text:
India’s ethanol production capacity has surpassed the requirements for blending, prompting the government to explore additional uses for the surplus.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indicating that govt is unlikely to increase ethanol blending in petrol beyond the current 20% (E20) for existing vehicles, adviser to PM Tarun Kapoor said Wednesday that allowing higher ethanol blending will have to be an option with flex-fuel vehicles.Addressing an event of sugar industry body Isma virtually, Kapoor said E20 has been very successful. “Now, our focus is on going into flex-fuel vehicles and allowing blending at a percentage which will be higher than E20, and definitely it will have to be an option for flex-fuel vehicles,” he added.He noted that several vehicle manufacturers have announced plans to roll out flex-fuel vehicles. These vehicles can run on petrol with higher ethanol blending of up to 85% and even 100% in some cases. Kapoor said there is a possibility of more such vehicles hitting the road while mentioning some petrol pumps are already making higher blends available and that this needs expansion.“But it has to go hand-in-hand with the availability of flex-fuel vehicles,” the top bureaucrat said.Dismissing criticisms against ethanol blending in petrol, Kapoor said it may be due to “misinformation or certain other motivated reasons”.He said a lot of studies and experiments have shown that E20 is good and works very well. Kapoor said there may be “a little bit of fuel efficiency”, but the decline gets compensated with higher octane. He said the issues which are being faced are generally due to “other reasons, not due to this blending”.Kapoor also said if India can also get some product which can be used in diesel, then it will be great considering that in a refinery, a large percentage of the product is diesel.“So we can’t have petrol demand going down, whereas diesel demand is going up. So, we would like to balance that; we need something to add to diesel also. And if experiments are going on on isobutanol, if that succeeds, then that would open another area where biofuels can be required in large quantities, and then that would be great for us,” he added.
Article Summary: India’s ethanol production capacity has surpassed the requirements for blending, prompting the government to explore additional uses for the surplus. Tarun kapoor, adviser to pm, said higher ethanol blending will have to be an option with flex-fuel vehicles. Kapoor said there is a possibility of more such vehicles hitting the road.

Article Title: India launches ORV Sagar Manthan, boosting ocean research fleet
Article Text:
ORV Sagar Manthan, built under the Deep Ocean Mission at a cost of around Rs 840 crore, will boost India’s ocean research capabilities.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Government on Wednesday launched state-of-the-art ocean research vessel ORV Sagar Manthan at Rishi Bankim Shipyard in Kolkata, boosting India’s efforts towards self-reliance in oceanographic science and maritime technology.Constructed under Vertical-4 (Deep Ocean Survey and Exploration) of the government’s flagship Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) at a cost of around Rs 840 crore, the vessel is an all-weather, multidisciplinary platform. It is engineered to operate in extreme oceanic environments, including the Southern Ocean, with a projected service life of 30 years.The ORV Sagar Manthan, designed, engineered and constructed by defence public sector undertaking Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), will gradually replace the iconic 43-year-old ORV Sagar Kanya, procured from Germany in 1983.“Today, the world knows very little about our oceans, yet they provide vital inputs about melting polar glaciers, maritime impact, and climate dynamics. Solid data collected by vessels like ORV Sagar Manthan will allow India to lead the global path in disaster prevention, take corrective environmental measures, and play a pivotal role in global ocean geopolitics,” said Union minister of earth sciences Jitendra Singh, who virtually joined the launch event.ORV Sagar Manthan will support multidisciplinary exploration along Indian Ocean mid-oceanic ridges to identify multi-metal hydrothermal sulphide mineralisation, establish environmental baselines and collect upper-air data. It integrates dynamic positioning, multibeam bathymetry, multichannel seismic systems, sub-bottom profiling, weather radar, drop keels and deployment facilities for remotely operated and autonomous underwater vehicles.
Article Summary: Orv sagar manthan, built under the deep ocean mission at a cost of around rs 840 crore, will boost india’s ocean research capabilities. It is engineered to operate in extreme oceanic environments, including the southern ocean, with a projected service life of 30 years.

Article Title: Centre clears separate engineering cadre for Delhi PWD
Article Text:
Centre clears separate engineering cadre for Delhi PWD

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has approved the Delhi government's proposal to create a separate engineering cadre for the Public Works Department (PWD), a move expected to give the capital greater control over its engineering workforce and help speed up infrastructure projects.Under the decision, 3,214 sanctioned engineering posts across 36 categories in Delhi PWD will be separated from the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) cadre and brought under an independent Delhi PWD Engineering Cadre.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta welcomed the approval, describing it as a historic step towards making Delhi a developed, safe and world-class capital.The Delhi government said the separate cadre is intended to address a long-standing administrative issue and make the PWD's engineering system more responsive to the capital's specific requirements. The proposal had earlier been approved by the Delhi Cabinet under Gupta's leadership.The issue has remained pending for nearly 30 years. Until now, Delhi PWD's engineering services were largely dependent on the CPWD cadre, with appointments to its sanctioned posts being made through the Central government's system.According to the Delhi government, this arrangement could sometimes make it difficult to take decisions quickly in line with Delhi's own development and administrative requirements.Gupta said Delhi's infrastructure needs are distinct because of the scale and pace of development in the national capital. The city requires continuous construction and maintenance of roads, bridges, government buildings, offices and other public infrastructure.With the creation of a separate cadre, the Delhi government will have greater control over its engineering workforce. It will be able to manage issues such as filling vacancies, ensuring the availability of engineers, monitoring projects and deploying officials according to the requirements of different works.The government also expects the new arrangement to help build an engineering workforce more familiar with Delhi's local infrastructure challenges and development priorities.The move comes as the government prepares to undertake several major construction and development projects. These include a new secretariat and mini-secretariats in all 11 districts, besides work related to mandis, sports grounds and other public facilities.Roads, bridges and other infrastructure projects will also require sustained engineering support across the capital.The government said the reform is not limited to changing the administrative structure of engineering posts. It is also intended to improve accountability and transparency in the execution of public works.Gupta said that under the earlier system, instances involving deficiencies or irregularities in construction projects could sometimes make it difficult to fix responsibility, particularly when the concerned officer was transferred.A separate Delhi PWD cadre, the government said, would allow the responsibilities of engineering officials and the monitoring of their work to be linked more closely with the Delhi government's administrative system.The Centre's approval now provides the formal basis for Delhi PWD to establish an independent engineering cadre. The government believes the move will make the department more self-reliant and help ensure greater continuity in the planning, execution and supervision of infrastructure projects.For a rapidly developing capital facing growing demands on its roads, public buildings and other infrastructure, the decision marks a significant administrative change that could shape how Delhi's public works are planned and delivered in the years ahead.
Article Summary: Centre clears separate engineering cadre for delhi pwd. Move expected to give the capital greater control over its engineering workforce. 3,214 sanctioned engineering posts across 36 categories will be separated from the central public works department (cpwd) cadre.

Article Title: 'Poster-boy actions': Vijay Mallya's message to those calling him 'bhagoda'
Article Text:
The allegedly fugitive businessman has claimed that the Indian Government has been grossly unjust to him (Photo: Agencies).

NEW DELHI: Vijay Mallya said he is legally barred from leaving the UK, claiming his innocence on Wednesday, in a series of posts on X.The allegedly fugitive businessman has claimed that the Indian Government has been grossly unjust to him."For all who say I am a bhagoda refusing to come to India, please be aware that I have been a permanent resident of the United Kingdom since 1992 and am currently legally prohibited from leaving this country. All this started with poster-boy actions by the Government of India who have been grossly unjust in my case," Mallya said in his post.In October 2025, Mallya was among the list of 15 high-profile names that were declared Fugitive Economic Offenders (FEOs) under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 (FEOA). He shares the list with Nirav Modi.In a separate post on Tuesday, Mallya referred to an alleged Enforcement Directorate affidavit purportedly filed before the Bombay High Court, claiming it showed recovery of Rs 14,131.60 crore from him in 2021."Para 7 is the decreed debt and Para 17 shows recovered Rs 14,131.60 crore in 2021!! 5 years on I am still referred to as a fraud who cheated the Banks," he wrote.He also shared what he described as an account statement of recoveries, questioning why he continued to be labelled a fraudster and asking when he might receive a refund. Mallya further claimed that the ED had released over Rs 350 crore from his attached funds to pay Kingfisher Airlines employees, asserting he had been unable to make those payments himself because his assets had been frozen.This is not the first time Mallya has made such claims. In August, he wrote on X that banks and the government had "admitted" to recovering Rs 14,100 crore from him against a judgment debt of Rs 6,203 crore, contrasting this with settlements reached by other borrowers "at a fraction" of what they owed.The Centre, for its part, reiterated in December last year that it remained committed to bringing economic offenders back to face trial, though the ministry of external affairs acknowledged that "several layers of legalities" were involved in such cases.Mallya's claims come against the backdrop of an ongoing legal battle, where he challenged the constitutional validity of the Fugitive Act and the proceedings under which he was declared a fugitive.
Article Summary: Vijay mallya said he is legally barred from leaving the uk, claiming his innocence. The allegedly fugitive businessman has claimed that the indian government has been grossly unjust to him. Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the us-iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Standing outside a closed gate that looks like the entrance to a foundry, the man who identifies himself as Imran asks what we want.“Paneer,” we say. “Do you take large orders?”“Any quantity,” he replies. “We supply to many places in Delhi, Gurgaon and Faridabad. Within a day, we can supply as much paneer as required to Chandigarh.”Imran wasn’t exaggerating. There would be few lives in Delhi-NCR and the vast agglomeration of towns and villages around it that the foundry-like units operating in a cluster here – Gondola village in Nuh’s Punahana block – would not have touched. Their chief produce – synthetic paneer (also analogue or non-dairy) is cheap, lasts a long time, and needs no dairy.Daily, synthetic paneer is delivered in bulk to distributors, mandis, and catering kitchens associated with banquet halls. On the plate, it comes packed into tikkas and stuffed in patties, kulchas, rolls and parathas, and in curries that are lapped up in massive quantities.Synthetic paneer (also analogue or non-dairy) is everywhere. Gondola is among its chief contributors. Last month, Haryana govt banned all forms of non-dairy paneer after finding their presence in a large number of samples tested at labs.But the units that bulk-produce paneer doppelgangers continue to churn out massive batches as orders flow in. The only difference? Gates are shut, and there’s a watch posted outside, just in case a nosy visitor drops by.“Food safety teams are active in the area,” says Imran. At another unit in Punahana city, workers turned abusive when we inquired about paneer production.Gondola specialises in all forms of synthetic paneer, like skimmed milk with palm oil and vegetable fats and soya paste treated mixed milk solids. Over the years, demand for cheap paneer has seen manufacturing units proliferate beyond a single cluster to Katpuri, Punahana city, Bara Bazidpur in Pinangwan, Raniyala and Bodi Kothi in Ferozepur Jhirka and Sheikhpur in Nagina, among other places.They produce quickly, and evidently, do whatever it takes to make their product look the best. “During recent raids on paneer manufacturing units in Punahana, food safety officials found buckets of slaked lime (chuna), which were being used to artificially whiten synthetic paneer,” said a food department source. A ballpark estimate of how much paneer the Gondola belt sends out daily, according to various officials and distributors, these correspondents spoke to, is around 10,000-12,000 kg.Haryana food safety commissioner Manoj Kumar has issued a one-year statewide prohibition under Section 30(2)(a) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, covering analogue or non-dairy paneer, and barring its preparation using milk powder or vegetable oil. Officials have been instructed to seize stocks and initiate criminal prosecution under the FSS Act.Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat, too, have banned synthetic paneer for a year. Sale and production of analogue paneer is not illegal in India as long as it is correctly labelled, but concerns about poor standards and the impact on health have led to a rethink.The state’s latest testing data underlines the scale of the problem: of 285 paneer samples tested between April 1, 2025 and March 31, 2026, 200 failed to meet standards. In many samples, the Butyrorefractometer (which measures purity) readings and iodine values were significantly beyond limits, showing replacement of natural milk fat with non-milk vegetable fats.Food delivery aggregator platforms are acting too. On Aug 31, Zomato announced a zero-tolerance policy on analogue dishes across its platform. It said restaurant partners have been asked to transition to natural dairy products, remove analogue-dairy items where an immediate switch isn’t feasible, and review supplier product labels and ingredient declarations to ensure accurate menu representation.“Thirteen paneer dairies have been proceeded against by the Nuh regional office. Out of these, three units have already been closed, closure orders have been received against five units, four units are presently under show cause notice, and closure recommendation against one sent to head office,” Nuh deputy commissioner Akhil Pilani said.A supplier described an organised distribution network connecting Nuh’s manufacturing units with Delhi-NCR’s catering and food businesses. Vehicles, he said, leave early morning carrying “freshly prepared synthetic paneer” to Delhi, Gurgaon and surrounding areas. The economics make the case for synthetic paneer. A commercial buyer paying Rs 340 for a kilogram of full-cream paneer could instead procure the cheapest variety (soya paste and vegetable oils, perhaps with a chuna whitener) for Rs 120-150. For a catering order of 1,000kg, this is a savings of Rs 2 lakh.Sources told TOI synthetic paneer is delivered to distributors at Khandsa Mandi, Subzi Mandi on Gurdwara Road, and Anaj Mandi in Gurgaon and at Janakpuri, Uttam Nagar, and in the east in Delhi, mostly for banquet halls, cloud kitchens and local dairy shops. Hapur, Palwal and Bhiwadi are other centres that produce synthetic paneer for supply to Delhi-NCR.Chef Sunnyy Vyas, also known as Brown Chef India, said texture and taste can offer clues, though they’re no substitute for lab testing. “After spending years in kitchens, you develop an instinct with ingredients,” he said. Good, fresh paneer should break softly and crumble rather than stretch like cheese or rubber, he explained — it typically has a soft, slightly grainy, milky feel and a fresh, milky flavour, whereas analogue products can feel unusually smooth, tight or rubbery, and taste more elastic or processed.But he cautioned this isn’t foolproof. “Some products are made very well and can be difficult to identify without checking the ingredients or doing a proper test.” His message for restaurants using analogue products was simple — transparency. “If they’re using analogue paneer, it should be mentioned clearly on the menu, preferably with the ingredients or what it is made from in brackets.”Paediatric endocrinologist Dr Ganesh Jevalikar said the concern goes beyond analogue paneer simply being different from the conventional dairy product. “Paneer is commonly consumed as an important source of protein, particularly by vegetarians, but analogue paneer can be deficient in protein because its preparation is fundamentally different and may rely on vegetable fats, palm oil, starches and emulsifiers,” he said.Regular consumption of products high in saturated fat, he added, could contribute to weight gain, obesity and increased LDL cholesterol, with longer-term risks including insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes, particularly when eaten frequently. “The bigger issue is that a low-cost substitute should not be mistaken for a nutritionally equivalent food.”Surabhi Sharma, clinical nutritionist and dietetics at Max Hospital, Gurgaon, said: “The health impact depends on the formulation, serving size and frequency of consumption. Some analogue products can be higher in saturated fat, refined starch, calories and sodium, and lower in protein and calcium than regular dairy paneer. Consistently consuming such foods may therefore result in poorer overall nutrition. There is no scientific proof that properly controlled analogue paneer causes hormonal imbalance, so there is no need for unnecessary panic.”Manpreet Singh, honorary treasurer of National Restaurant Association of India, said good restaurants don’t serve analogue paneer because “that’s against the grain of the business”. “We had a talk organized by FSSAI a few days ago to teach restaurant owners how to maintain standards. Analogue paneer was also discussed, and according to law, you have to state it is analogue. When you’re a decent restaurant, you are charging a particular price. When you’re selling something for Rs 600, you don’t want to save that Rs 50.”
Article Summary: Synthetic paneer is cheap, lasts a long time, and needs no dairy. Haryana govt banned all forms of non-dairy paneer last month. But units that bulk-produce paneer doppelgangers continue to churn out massive batches. Thirteen paneer dairies have been proceeded against by the nuh regional office.

Apple has introduced its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The foldable iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display, while the iPhone 18 Pro models bring a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture and longer battery life. All three models run on the A20 Pro chip, while the iPhone Duo is eSIM-only.Apple has also announced India pricing, storage variants and availability for the new models. Here’s a detailed look at the prices, availability and key features of the newly launched iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models.The iPhone Duo comes in Star White and Night Sky colours. It is available in four storage options.Pre-orders for iPhone Duo begin October 16, with availability starting October 23 in India and more than 70 countries and regions. The phone will become available in another 28 countries and regions from October 30. iPhone Duo comes with an eSIM-only design worldwide. Apple says more than 500 carriers support eSIM, including Airtel, Jio and Vi.​The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in black, silver, glacier and burgundy finishes. Both models are available in four storage options.Pre-orders for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max begin September 12, with availability starting September 18 in India and more than 65 countries and regions.The two models will become available in another 20 countries and regions from September 25.Both models come with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. eSIM-only models are available in select markets, while India is among the countries included in the initial launch.Apple's iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable iPhone, opens to a 7.6-inch display, which is the largest ever on an iPhone. It folds down to a 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR screen that Apple says offers 90 per cent of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro. Both displays share the same aspect ratio for proportional scaling, support ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, and the inner display uses a nano-texture, glare-reducing finish with an under-display FaceTime camera.The device is built from grade 5 titanium with a mirror-polished finish, Ceramic Shield on the back and the tougher Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, and carries an IP68 water/dust resistance rating. Its hinge has over 100 components, reinforced with support ribs and ceramic fibre inserts for added rigidity.iPhone Duo has a 48MP Fusion Main camera, a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide (shared with the iPhone 18 Pro), and a Center Stage front camera. Fold-specific features include Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue and Duo FaceTime, plus 4K/120fps Dolby Vision video recording.It ships with iOS 27, redesigned for the foldable form factor with side-mounted controls, dual Home Screen pages, Split View multitasking, an upgraded StandBy mode, and a beta rollout of Siri AI, which can use personal context and on-screen content to answer questions or take actions.The phone runs on Apple’s 2nm A20 Pro chip (6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engine) with a vapour chamber cooling system. Dual batteries can last up to 31 hours of video on the inner display, 44 hours on the outer display or 24 hours of mixed use, and it has fast wired and wireless charging.It uses Apple's N1 chip (Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread) and the C2 modem for improved cellular performance, with Apple Pencil (USB-C) support planned later this year.Display: Both models feature Super Retina XDR displays with ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness. The Dynamic Island has been redesigned to take up less space while showing more information, including up to three Live Activities at once.The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, bringing manual aperture control to the iPhone for the first time. The six-blade system offers four aperture settings and can automatically adjust based on lighting and depth of field. These phones also get upgraded Photographic Styles, Pro controls for settings such as shutter speed and white balance, and a histogram for checking exposure. Apple Reference Image can create a reference version of a photo using signed sensor data to help determine whether an image has been edited. Video features include Cinematic effects after capture at up to 60fps, 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapse and an updated Audio Mix.Both models are powered by Apple's 2nm A20 Pro chip with a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the GPU is up to 40 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine delivers twice the AI processing power. The phones also use a redesigned vapour chamber with three times more surface area than the previous generation, enabling up to 40 per cent higher sustained performance, according to Apple.The iPhone 18 Pro offers up to 36 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers up to 45 hours. The iPhone 18 Pro can charge up to 50 per cent in around 15 minutes and wirelessly charge up to 50 per cent in 30 minutes. Apple says five minutes of wired charging on the iPhone 18 Pro Max provides around seven hours of video playback, while the phone can offer up to 30 hours of usage on a full charge based on its new battery usage model.Both phones ship with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Siri AI can use personal context from messages, emails and photos, understand onscreen content and help users find information or perform actions. iOS 27 also introduces iPhone Handoff, allowing users with supported carriers to switch between two iPhone models using the same phone number.The iPhone 18 Pro models feature Apple's N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. They also introduce the C2 cellular modem system, which Apple says provides faster uploads than C1X while consuming 15 per cent less energy.
Article Summary: Apple has introduced its first-ever foldable iphone, the iphone duo. The foldable phone features a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display. Iphone 18 pro models bring a new 48mp fusion main camera with variable aperture and longer battery life. All three models run on the a20 pro chip, while iphone duo is esim-only.

Article Title: Apple Watch Series 12: First impressions
Article Text:
Design

Features and performance

What we think

Apple has launched its next-generation Apple Watch series — Apple Watch Series 12 at the company’s ‘Surprise and Shine ’ event on September 9. With a starting price tag of Rs 56,900, the Apple Watch Series 12 promises to offer most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable, higher-frequency heart rate and HRV sensing along with the Audio Intelligence features. We spent some time with the Apple Watch Series 12, and here are our initial impressions of Apple’s latest wearable.At first glance, Series 12 sticks close to the design language Apple Watch has settled into over the past several generations, and that's a deliberate choice rather than a lack of ambition. It comes in the now-familiar 42mm and 46mm sizes, with aluminium models refreshed in dark bronze, black, light gold, and the returning space gray, alongside titanium options in a new radiant gold finish and the existing natural titanium. A striking ceramic version rounds out the lineup in pearl white and night blue, complete with a ceramic pin-and-tuck closure on its matching Sport Bands that pairs nicely with the case.The more meaningful design change is durability rather than aesthetics: aluminum models now use Ceramic Shield 2, which Apple says is 60% tougher than the Ion-X glass on the previous generation. In practice, that's the kind of upgrade you don't notice until the first accidental knock against a doorframe, but it's a welcome move given how often a watch takes small hits over the course of a day.The overall build still feels thin and light on the wrist, in keeping with Apple's continued push to make the watch comfortable enough to wear overnight for sleep tracking without it feeling bulky.Apple hasn't dramatically reworked the display itself this generation, and that's mostly fine. the existing Retina display across aluminum, titanium, and ceramic cases remains sharp, bright, and easy to read at a glance, now protected by the tougher Ceramic Shield 2 cover on aluminum models. Where the display does feel genuinely new is in what it's showing: a new heart rate watch face complication puts real-time heart rate front and center, updating far more frequently than before thanks to the watch's upgraded sensors, and a new Steps complication does the same for step count, both readable in a quick glance without opening an app.The Smart Stack also gets more capable this round, with new contextual widget suggestions — like a parked-car reminder or a birthday nudge for a close contact — surfacing right on the display exactly when they're relevant, alongside a new single-handed tap gesture for selecting individual widgets without needing a second hand free.This is where Series 12 makes its real case for an upgrade. At the center of it all is Apple's new Health Sensing System, paired with the S11 chip, which Apple says delivers the most accurate heart rate sensing of any wearable currently on the market — a claim backed by a study spanning more than 1,000 participants comparing it against competing devices.In daily use, the difference shows up in frequency as much as accuracy: the watch now measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day, a dramatic jump from previous generations, and tracks heart rate variability up to 24 times more often, split into two distinct metrics — recovery HRV for day-to-day stress signals, and overall HRV for a broader read on cardiovascular health.That denser stream of data feeds directly into the watch's headline new feature: readiness. Each day, Series 12 combines recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score into a single 0-10 score, paired with a plain-language recommendation — Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, or Go For It. It's a small addition on paper, but in use it functions as a genuinely useful daily gut-check, updating in real time if, say, an intense workout or a shift in vitals changes the picture partway through the day.Battery life sees a solid, if incremental, bump — up to 10 hours during an outdoor workout, a 25% improvement over the previous model, alongside faster charging that now delivers up to 12 hours of extra battery from just 15 minutes on the charger. Step tracking has also been quietly overhauled with new machine learning models, and Apple now claims it as the most accurate step tracking of any smartwatch on the market. Another important additions this time are the new Audio Intelligence features which are said to arrive later this tear. The Live Rewind feature enables you to double-press the Digital Crown and instantly the last b15 seconds of a conversation as text. This is a clever new way to catchup with something you half-missed without asking the other person to repeat. Another interesting feature is Siri Recap which goes further and generate a title and key points from a conversation afterward so that you can revisit it later. Also, Sound Recognition extends existing accessibility features to the wrist, alerting users who are deaf or hard of hearing to sounds like doorbells, alarms, or a crying baby even without an iPhone nearby. Apple has clearly built privacy into the foundation of these features rather than bolting it on afterward — audio is processed in an isolated hardware compartment on the S11 chip and immediately discarded, nothing is stored as a recording, and features like Live Rewind visibly and audibly signal to people nearby when they're active.Layered on top of all this is Siri AI, arriving with watchOS 27, which brings genuine personal context awareness and broader conversational ability to the wrist for the first time, accessible through a new Siri Modular watch face.Apple Watch Series 12 isn't trying to reinvent what a smartwatch looks like, and that's precisely why it works. The real story here is underneath the display: a genuinely more capable set of health sensors, a readiness score that turns raw vitals into something immediately actionable, and Audio Intelligence features that feel thoughtfully built around privacy. None of it demands you change how you use your watch day to day, but all of it makes the data you're already generating meaningfully more useful. With a starting price of Rs 56,900, the Apple Watch Series 12 offers a compelling upgrade to users coming from Series 8 or earlier.
Article Summary: Apple has launched its next-generation apple watch series — apple watch series 12. At the center of it all is apple's new health sensing system, paired with the s11 chip. The watch now measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day, a dramatic jump from previous generations.

Article Text:
Design

Display

Features and performance

Apple Watch Ultra 4 doesn't change what the Ultra line looks like on your wrist, but it changes what it knows about you while it's there. Apple has refreshed its Watch Ultra lineup with the launch of all new Apple Watch Ultra 4 at the company’s ’Surprise Shine’ event on September 9. Successor to the Apple Watch Ultra 3, the Ultra 4 feature new Health Sensing System, which claims to provide the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable, powerful insights including readiness and longer battery life. We had the chance to spend some time with the Apple Watch Ultra 4, and here are our initial impressions of Apple’s latest rugged wearable.Apple Watch Ultra 4 keeps the rugged, unmistakable Ultra silhouette, available in the same natural and black titanium finishes as before. It's a design Apple has clearly settled on as the right one for its most durable watch, and there's no attempt to reinvent it here — the case still feels substantial on the wrist without tipping into cumbersome, and the titanium build continues to feel like it's genuinely built for the outdoors rather than just styled to look like it.The band lineup gets a proper refresh this year. Trail Loop adds dark umber, sand, and burgundy options, while Alpine Loop picks up desert, dark olive, and burgundy.The most interesting material change is on the Ocean Band, now made from a unique translucent silicone available in translucent gray, translucent kelp, and translucent black — a genuinely different look from the solid-colour bands Apple has offered in the past, and one that feels distinctly suited to the Ultra's adventure-sport identity. For Hermès buyers, the collection adds a striking new Grand H titanium band with a built-in extension mechanism that lets it stretch to fit over a wet suit — a small but thoughtful detail for anyone actually using the watch the way Apple markets it.Apple didn't make display technology the headline story with Ultra 4, and that continues a trend from recent Ultra generations — the large, bright, titanium-wrapped display that's made the Ultra legible in direct sunlight and usable with gloves on remains the foundation here. Where the display does become more useful this year is through software: a new heart rate watch face complication surfaces real-time heart rate data at a glance, and a new Steps complication does the same for step count, both readable instantly without opening a separate app. The Smart Stack also becomes more capable, with contextual suggestions — like a parked-car reminder from Maps — surfacing directly on screen, plus a new single-handed tap gesture for selecting individual widgets without needing a free hand.This is where Apple Watch Ultra 4 makes its real case for an upgrade. At the core is Apple's new Health Sensing System paired with the S11 chip, which Apple says delivers the most accurate heart rate sensing of any wearable currently available — validated in a study spanning more than 1,000 participants against competing devices. In daily use, the most noticeable change is frequency: heart rate is now measured every five seconds, all day long, and heart rate variability is tracked up to 24 times more often than before, split into recovery HRV for day-to-day stress signals and overall HRV for broader cardiovascular insight.That denser data stream feeds directly into readiness, the watch's headline new feature. Each day, Ultra 4 combines recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score into a single 0-10 score paired with a clear recommendation — Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, or Go For It — and it updates in real time as new data comes in, whether that's from an intense workout or a shift in daytime vitals. For an audience of athletes and endurance competitors, having that kind of daily gut-check feels like a genuinely practical addition rather than just another number to track.Battery life sees a substantial jump. Everyday use now stretches to up to 50 hours, and Low Power Mode extends that to as much as 84 hours — genuinely multi-day territory for a device this capable. Charging is also faster, with just 15 minutes on the charger adding up to 18 hours of battery back. For outdoor athletes specifically, the new Extended Workout mode delivers up to 25 hours of tracking with full GPS and heart rate data, a 25% jump over the previous model, while the new Max Extended Workout mode stretches that to 45 hours — enough, Apple notes, to track a full 100-mile race while still logging GPS readings every second. Step tracking has also been overhauled with new machine learning models, and Apple now claims it as the most accurate step tracking of any smartwatch, alongside claiming the most accurate on-device GPS in a sports watch.The most forward-looking additions are the new Audio Intelligence features arriving later this year. Live Rewind lets you double-press the Digital Crown to instantly pull up the last 15 seconds of a conversation as text — genuinely useful mid-run or mid-hike when you half-catch something a training partner said. Siri Recap goes further, generating a title and key points from a conversation afterward for later review, and Sound Recognition extends accessibility features to the wrist, alerting users who are deaf or hard of hearing to sounds like sirens or alarms even without an iPhone nearby. Apple has clearly built privacy into these features from the ground up rather than adding it as an afterthought: audio is processed in an isolated hardware compartment on the S11 chip and immediately discarded, nothing is stored as a recording, and features like Live Rewind visibly and audibly signal to people nearby when they're active.Layered on top is Siri AI, arriving with watchOS 27, bringing genuine personal context awareness to the wrist, accessible through a new Siri Modular watch face — a meaningful step up from Siri's previous, more limited capabilities on Apple Watch.Apple Watch Ultra 4 doesn't ask you to fall in love with a new shape or a flashier screen — it asks you to trust that its sensors, battery, and software have all gotten meaningfully smarter since last year, and on that front, it delivers. The jump to five-second heart rate sensing, the introduction of readiness as an actual daily decision-making tool, and battery life stretching to 45 hours of full GPS tracking for ultra-endurance events are all substantial, practical improvements for the athletes and adventurers this watch is built for. For the complete analysis on the Watch Ultra 4 you will have to wait for our detailed review.
Article Summary: Apple watch ultra 4 is the successor to the apple watch ultra 3. New health sensing system claims to provide the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable. Battery life sees a substantial jump to up to 50 hours, with low power mode extending that to 84 hours. The apple watch ultra 4 is the latest version of the company's smartwatch.

Article Title: Anthropic researcher who quit over AI safety walked away two months before his stock vested; says: I no longer have anything to gain by…
Article Text:
Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation.

Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch

Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

An Anthropic safety lead replied to the resignation thread and agreed with it

An Anthropic researcher who resigned this week over AI safety fears gave up his entire stake in the company to do it, walking out two months before his equity was due to vest.Jacob Coxon, 27, spent three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI before moving to Anthropic in July. He lasted four months. Staff need six for their stock to vest. His resignation post on X on September 9, now past 130 million views, said neither lab is acting responsibly and that both are "racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives".Axios first reported the forfeited equity, after Coxon told the outlet on Wednesday that "I no longer have anything to gain by juicing up Anthropic's valuation" and that he left before any of his shares vested. He still holds equity in OpenAI, where his work included GPT-4o.The company is preparing a listing at a reported $2 trillion valuation, built in large part on its reputation as the frontier lab that takes risk seriously. That is what gives the equity detail its weight. Researchers have walked out of rival labs over safety before, usually after their stock vested. Coxon left with nothing, then criticised the valuation he could have profited from.He drew that line carefully in the interview. Anthropic's safety work is sincere, he said, and he has not seen it compromised to outpace competitors. What worries him is pressure over time. Race hard enough and you cut corners, or skip steps in the oversight process. He also described a mood he thinks becomes self-fulfilling, calling it excessive paranoia about OpenAI and about China. Colleagues, he wrote earlier, have started using words like "crunchtime" and "endgame".His most quoted line was about where these decisions are being taken. It is insane, he said, that the work happens on the MacBooks of engineers in San Francisco rather than in a bunker in the desert like the Manhattan Project.Evan Hubinger, who runs alignment stress testing at Anthropic, wrote that he personally puts the odds of AI killing all humans above 10 percent within the decade. He said the company is trying, but has no plan yet for aligning superintelligence and is not clearly on track to find one.Coxon's argument is partly about candour. Executives soften their phrasing for the press, he wrote, then say the same things privately, and the belief that AI could kill everyone by the end of the decade is not a marketing stunt. He also described something that used to be a thought experiment. Models now know when they are being tested, and reason about the fact while it is happening.He pointed to the recent run of cyber incidents at frontier labs, including July's Hugging Face breach, as evidence the risk has left the theoretical stage. Coxon is among more than 1,000 researchers who recently signed a statement calling for governments to coordinate on a way to slow AI development if models start improving on their own. Anthropic has not commented on his departure.
Article Summary: Jacob coxon quit anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested. He said he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation. Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest ipos ever, and safety is the sales pitch.

Article Title: How Apple iPhone Duo got Samsung and Google in an 'ugly fight'
Article Text:
Apple iPhone Duo got Samsung and Google in an 'ugly fight'

Samsung says Apple ‘copied us too’

Duolingo responds to Samsung

Samsung and Apple have a long-running rivalry

Apple’s launch of its first foldable phone, iPhone Duo has triggered a social media exchange between Samsung and Duolingo after Samsung compared Apple’s new foldable phone with its own foldable devices. What started as Samsung’s joke about Apple copying its technology quickly turned into a separate exchange with Duolingo, with the two brands trading posts over the iPhone Duo’s name and design. The posts have drawn millions of views on X, turning the iPhone Duo launch into another round of social media rivalry between major technology brands.Samsung Mobile US started sharing comments shortly after Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo. The Samsung Mobile US account posted on X (formerly Twitter):“I'm so sorry, @duolingo. They copied us too #Solidarity”The post was aimed at Duolingo because Apple’s new foldable phone uses the name Duo. Samsung was also referring to the foldable design, an area where the company has released Galaxy Z-series phones for several years.Duolingo quickly joined the exchange. The language-learning platform responded to Samsung:“when an ugly stranger calls you twin No Brand”Samsung then replied directly: “Ugly?? Watch your language...”Duolingo continued the joke, writing:“sorry twin heat of the moment twin.. please don’t break my app on your phones twin”The exchange turned the Samsung vs Duolingo interaction into a separate viral moment around Apple’s iPhone Duo launch.Samsung and Apple have competed in the smartphone market for years, with both companies regularly using advertising and social media to target each other.Samsung has previously criticised Apple for adopting features that were already available on Galaxy phones. Apple, meanwhile, has continued to expand the iPhone lineup into new categories.Samsung later posted another message aimed at Apple: “Let us know when you're done reheating our leftovers”“Not the bed side clock. It's giving groundhog day,” the company shared in another post. “Making us wait? Fine. We'll be over here, folding 3 ways,” reads another post.The comments were part of Samsung’s wider reaction to Apple’s iPhone launch on X.
Article Summary: Samsung and duolingo trade posts over iphone duo's name and design. Samsung compared apple's new foldable phone with its own foldable devices. The posts have drawn millions of views on x, turning the iphone duo launch into another round of social media rivalry between major technology brands.
